rival.derby: the Derby of the Eternal Enemies
rival.framing: friendly — the port against the city centre

coldOpen.line: For three whole seasons, nobody in Greece could beat them. Thirty-six games. Thirty wins. Not one defeat.
coldOpen.reveal: Unbeaten against every Greek team from March 1926 to March 1929 — and the newspapers called them Thrylos, the Legend, for the first time. The six titles in a row of the 1950s made the name stick for ever.

beats.line: Born in 1925 in the port of Piraeus, from two older clubs of the port; a naval officer, Notis Kamperos, proposed the name and the emblem.
beats.conflict: Wikipedia also gives a 1924 founding meeting; the club celebrates 10 March 1925 — narrate 1925

beats.line: The badge is a laurel-crowned youth — an Olympic victor.

beats.rule: Anastopoulos' moustache and Đorđević's left foot are fine as art; every narrated claim needs a source

beats.line: Gate 7 — painted as a red sea of flags, no flares.

ownerResearchCheck.claim: Founded by sailors, stevedores and dockworkers
ownerResearchCheck.verdict: not supported — founders were port townspeople (a navy officer, an industrialist, a merchant, a lawyer…); reframed

ownerResearchCheck.claim: 'Thrylos' came from beating foreign navy teams in the 1930s
ownerResearchCheck.verdict: not supported — the press first used it after the 1926–29 unbeaten run; replaced with the sourced story
